text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
English Doctor FREDERIC MANNING was born in 1839. In Australia he was remembered for his fight for modern, humane treatment of mentally ill people.
French Impressionist painter PIERRE AUGUSTE RENOIR was born on this day in 1841.

Australian cricketer GEORGE BONNOR (a renowned big-hitter) was born in 1855. The "big fellow" played in 17 Tests, could throw a ball more than 120 yards (109.7 metres), and is once said to have hit a ball so high that he took three runs before it hit the ground!

Italian opera singer ENRICO CARUSO, considered the greatest lyric tenor of his time, was born on this day in 1873. By 1924 he was so famous that the people of Naples dedicated a giant candle to him. 6-metres high and 2-metres wide, the candle is lit every year on his birthday, and is expected to last more
than a thousand years!
British pianist Dame MYRA HESS was born in 1890.
Australian athlete HERB ELLIOTT, who broke the 4-minute-mile 17 times and won Olympic Gold for the 1500 metres, was born on this day in 1938.
British film producer DAVID PUTTNAM was born in 1941.

British musician and former Beatle GEORGE HARRISON was born on this day in 1943. He began his career in the mid-fifties and joined his brother's group the 'Rebels'. A series of different bands followed and then finally in 1960 the Beatles. GEORGE wrote two of the group's more beautiful songs "Here Comes The Sun" and "Something". He also wrote "While My Guitar Gently Weeps". He had an international hit with "My Sweet Lord" (1970). Other solo hits included "Give Me Love (Give Me Peace On Earth)" (1973), , "All Those Years Ago" (1981) and "Got My Mind Set On You" (1987). He also worked with the 'Travelling Wilburys'. In recent years he has devoted time and energy to the production
company, Handmade Films.
** EVENTS **
1308 : King EDWARD II of England was crowned.
1570 : Queen ELIZABETH I of England was excommunicated by
POPE PIUS V.
1723 : Sir CHRISTOPHER WREN, English architect and
designer, died. He became a prolific designer of buildings following the Great Fire of London in 1666, notably of the new St Paul's cathedral.
1841 : Explorer EDWARD JOHN EYRE left Fowlers Bay in
South Australia on an overland trip around the Great Australian Bight. He reached Albany in July.
1862 : American President ABRAHAM LINCOLN introduced a
new version of the dollar bill (known as a "greenback"), to finance the Union's mounting Civil War costs.
1899 : PAUL JULIUS REUTER, German founder of the news
agency that bears his name, died. In 1850 he set up a pigeon post service from Aachen to Brussels to bridge the last gap in the expanding European telegraph system.
1913 : Federal income tax was introduced in the United
States.
1913 : EMMELINE PANKHURST, the founder of the British
suffragette movement, went on trial accused of bombing the villa of Chancellor of the Exchequer DAVID LLOYD GEORGE.
1914 : English artist Sir JOHN TENNIEL, best known for
his illustrations for "Alice in Wonderland", died.
1932 : Austrian-born ADOLF HITLER became a German
citizen.
1943 : In New Zealand 48 Japanese prisoners of war were

shot at the Featherston camp. Another 74 prisoners were injured in the prisoners' uprising. One guard was killed and six others were wounded. Officials said the Japanese were rebelling against work and did not understand that the 1929 Prisoners of War Convention provided for compulsory work.
1956 : In a sensational speech to the Communist Party
Congress, NIKITA KHRUSHCHEV denounced STALIN as a demigod and tyrant.
1964 : CASSIUS CLAY (MUHAMMAD ALI) won the world
heavyweight boxing crown, defeating SONNY LISTON in Miami Beach. Battered and injured after 6 rounds, LISTON refused to come out of his corner for the 7th!
1986 : CORAZON AQUINO defeated the right-wing dictator
FERDINAND MARCOS, to become President of the Philippines.
1988 : American television evangelist JIMMY SWAGGART was
banned from preaching for a year by the ASSEMBLIES OF GOD, after being photographed with a prostitute.
1989 : American heavyweight boxer MIKE TYSON defeated
British champion FRANK BRUNO.
1991 : 28 people were killed when a SCUD missile struck a
United States army barracks in Dhahran (Saudi Arabia), during the Persian Gulf War.
1996 : Moslem bombers killed 25 people and wounded 77 in
two revenge attacks in Israel.
